nodes.title: Keep game state in signals
nodes.why: The snake, both directions, food, score and the three status flags are signals, so the board, the status row and the Start/Pause label update after a key handler or the interval writes them, and tests read the same values through calls like snake() and direction().
nodes.alternative: Keep plain fields with default change detection, or derive game state from DOM classes.
nodes.tradeoff: Eight signals take more ceremony than fields, but every write the timer makes reaches the OnPush view without markForCheck().

nodes.title: Buffer at most one valid turn
nodes.why: Once a valid perpendicular turn occupies the buffer, bufferTurn returns it for every later key in the same tick, and same or opposite keys return null without taking the slot. onKeydown() passes the committed direction, so RIGHT → UP → LEFT commits UP.
nodes.alternative: Update direction immediately for every key press, or validate each key against the previous key.
nodes.tradeoff: Keys pressed after the first valid turn in a tick are dropped, which is the price of never reversing into the body.

nodes.title: Start exactly one game loop
nodes.why: start() returns early unless the game is paused and clears any old interval before creating one, so Start and Space never stack loops.
nodes.alternative: Move immediately on start or create a new interval every time Start is clicked.
nodes.tradeoff: Guarding and clearing the timer is a little ceremony, but it prevents duplicate loops and speed drift.

nodes.title: Reset from canonical constants
nodes.why: Reset must restore the same initial snake, direction, buffer, food, score and flags every time; copying the constant gives the signal a fresh array and leaves INITIAL_SNAKE untouched.
nodes.alternative: Try to undo the latest moves from the current snake state.
nodes.tradeoff: Constants make reset deterministic, but changing the initial scenario requires updating those constants intentionally.

nodes.title: Check the next head before changing the snake

anchor.snippet: const nextHead = { x: head.x + delta.x, y: head.y + delta.y };

nodes.why: stepSnake tests nextHead against the walls and the body first and, on a crash, returns outcome 'lost' with the old snake, so the board stays on the frame before the collision.
nodes.alternative: Move first, then inspect whether the new snake is invalid.
nodes.tradeoff: Pre-checks make the branches more explicit and keep the visible board frozen on the collision frame.

nodes.title: Grow on food, otherwise drop the tail
nodes.why: Movement is a head prepend plus a tail drop; eating keeps the tail and adds one to the score. Building a new array is also what lets snake.set() in the component notify the template.
nodes.alternative: Mutate the existing snake array in place, adding the head and popping the tail.
nodes.tradeoff: A new array per tick is a small allocation on a 14x14 board; an in-place edit would leave the signal holding the same reference, so the board would not update.

nodes.title: Represent a full board explicitly
nodes.why: placeFood picks only from free cells and returns null when none remain, so stepSnake reports 'won' and the component stops with a win instead of drawing food on the snake.
nodes.alternative: Pick random coordinates until one is not occupied.
nodes.tradeoff: Building a free-cell list is straightforward and bounded on a 14x14 board, while retry loops need extra safeguards.

nodes.title: Clear the timer when the component is destroyed
nodes.why: Angular can remove the component while the interval is still scheduled; the DestroyRef callback clears it, so no tick writes signals after teardown.
nodes.alternative: Implement ngOnDestroy, or rely on the browser to discard timers eventually.
nodes.tradeoff: Registering the cleanup in the constructor needs no lifecycle interface; ngOnDestroy does the same job as a separate method.

nodes.title: Write the engine result back into signals
nodes.why: tick() runs in a setInterval callback that no template event triggers. Writing signals marks the OnPush view for check, so the board moves on every tick; a plain field changed here would leave the view stale.
nodes.alternative: Keep plain fields and call ChangeDetectorRef.markForCheck() after each tick, or drop OnPush.
nodes.tradeoff: Five set() calls take more lines than one assignment, but a signal notifies only when its value changed, so a tick that only moves the snake does not notify score or food.

nodes.title: Derive the status label with computed
nodes.why: The label depends on three flags; computed recalculates it only when one of them changes, and the template reads statusLabel() instead of repeating the order win, game over, running.
nodes.alternative: Use a getter, which reruns on every change detection pass, or three @if blocks in the template.
nodes.tradeoff: One more class member, in exchange for a single place that decides a win outranks game over.
